lines.t: I came in with a heart bled dry,
Dragging every year behind me.
Old rooms, old names, old alibis,
All the things that formed and confined me.
I learned to laugh when the wound went deep,
Turn pain into a private language.
But silence knows what I could not speak,
And Your Spirit cuts through all my camouflage.
Don’t just touch the surface,
Don’t just soothe the bruise.
Pull the root out of me,
Even if it tears me loose.
I don’t want a little healing
That disappears when the night gets long.
I don’t want a borrowed feeling,
A temporary place to belong.
Take me to Your quiet place,
Where I cannot hide my face.
Let the truth undo me slow—
I need the whole restoration.
No partial light.
No half-way home.
You opened up the inward man,
Not to shame him, but to free him.
Every vow I made with shaking hands,
Every lie I let them teach him.
“You’ll be safe when nobody gets close.”
“You’ll be worthy when they want you.”
“You’ll be strong when you never need hope.”
Those were graves, not walls to run to.
I accept where I became cruel,
Where I ran, where I chose control.
But I will not call my chains “wisdom,”
I will not make a home in a hole.
I don’t want a little healing
That disappears when the night gets long.
I don’t want a borrowed feeling,
A temporary place to belong.
Take me to Your quiet place,
Where I cannot hide my face.
Let the truth undo me slow—
I need the whole restoration.
No partial light.
No half-way home.
In Your arms, the noise gets smaller.
In Your arms, I hear what is real.
Not the boy who had to earn love,
Not the man who learned not to feel.
There is no performance left between us,
No bargain, no deal, no disguise.
Only Your Spirit searching every chamber,
Only mercy holding open my eyes.
I do not want to know You only
As a thought that I repeat.
Make Your promise live inside me
Until my blood believes in peace.
Let what You have spoken settle
Past the mind and through the bone.
Make me whole where I am shattered—
Not someday.
Not in pieces.
Bring me home.
I don’t want a little healing
That disappears when the night gets long.
I don’t want a borrowed feeling,
A temporary place to belong.
Take me to Your quiet place,
Hold my ruined heart with grace.
Let the truth become my bones—
I need the whole restoration.
No partial light.
No half-way home.
A heart bled dry can learn to breathe.
A soul split wide can still receive.
In the quiet, I stop running.
In Your arms, I come undone.
And what You promised becomes real—
Not just words…
But where I live.
